## What is referral marketing?

[Referral marketing](https://www.referralcandy.com/referral-marketing/) is one of the most cost-effective marketing strategies: using your current customers to spread the word about your brand to new customers.

To turn your loyal customers into your biggest brand advocates, you have to make the referral process as easy as possible for them, and you have to stay top-of-mind with killer referral incentives, like free products and major discounts.

We compiled a truly epic list of the best referral program ideas currently on the market, along with recommendations on what kinds of referral program software to use, incentives to offer, and current customers to target for your very own referral program.

By the end of our list, you will have enough referral program ideas to launch your very own program and open the floodgates of another customer acquisition channel for your business.

Before we begin, let's break down some basic referral marketing definitions so that we know that we're all on the same page.

## What is a referral program?

A referral program or a “refer-a-friend” program is a marketing strategy used by many top ecommerce brands to incentivize existing customers to recommend the brand and its products to their family and friends.

A referral program is a deliberate, systematic way of getting people to make referrals to your business. Referral programs are often called word-of-mouth marketing, because they reward existing customers for sharing and incentivize new customers to try out your brand.

Customers are rewarded with [referral incentives](https://www.referralcandy.com/blog/referral-program-incentives/), such as free cash, major discounts, or a free month of subscription. While there is an upfront cost to the business, referral programs significantly increase long-term revenue by making loyal customers out of your existing customer base.

If you are wondering why you should have a referral program and how to run one, let’s take a look at how the top ecommerce brands are running their referral programs and the results they have achieved.

Before we begin, let's quickly go through the basics of referral programs.

## Why do I need a referral program?

One of the biggest stresses of any business is finding a solid [customer acquisition](https://www.referralcandy.com/blog/customer-acquisition-channels/) channel, or basically, bringing in new customers. When you have a solid referral marketing program, however, you let your existing customers bring new buyers to your brand. 

This not only significantly reduces spending on bringing new customers to your shop, but also increases customer retention, which is a very good thing.

Why?

**Because loyal customers have a higher conversion rate than new customers and spend more per transaction, making customer referral programs the most cost-effective and lucrative marketing strategy that your business can possibly employ.  
  
**

## How does a referral program work?

People don't make as many referrals as they intend to for a variety of reasons. A referral program helps make their mind up with a tangible reward for referrals.

Modern referral programs, or refer-a-friend programs, use software to track referrals made by happy customers through either a referral code, a rewards card, or a [referral link](https://www.referralcandy.com/blog/why-referral-links/).

Depending on the referral campaign, customers will usually receive some kind of referral bonus or benefit when they refer a friend. [Referral marketing software](https://www.referralcandy.com/referral-marketing/) automates the payout of these referral rewards.

This referral process creates a natural word-of-mouth marketing experience for your brand, which ultimately increases both your customer retention rate and your revenue.

To find out more, check out [how ReferralCandy works.](https://www.referralcandy.com/referral-marketing/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=47_referral_programs&utm_content=inline&utm_term=top)

## How do I create a referral program?

The best way to bring in potential customers is to first focus on your existing satisfied customers. Rather than just offering cash rewards or free gifts in hopes that your customers will refer a friend to your shop, it takes a little bit of planning to set up a referral program that works.

### 1\. Get clear about your goals

Before creating a complex ambassador program or launching tons of marketing campaigns (of any kind), it's important to be clear about what your goals are for the program. 

This will help guide you as you brainstorm referral marketing ideas. Some questions to consider are:

*   What are you hoping to get out of your rewards program?
*   Do you want more customers? Or just bigger purchases by your existing customers?
*   Are you trying to get a higher conversion rate and increase sales?

You can certainly achieve each of these goals, but it might require a different referral campaign for each goal. So it's important to be clear about your goals before beginning.

Affiliate Publishing and Referral Senior Content Manager

Read time: 10 mins

When a friend recommends a product or service, you listen—that’s the power behind every successful referral marketing strategy. Maybe you started watching Ted Lasso because colleagues wouldn’t stop talking about it, or downloaded Duolingo because a friend insisted it was life-changing. This isn’t coincidence—it’s the referral effect in action.

Market leaders like Tesla and Airbnb have built empires largely through [strategic word-of-mouth](https://impact.com/referral/word-of-mouth-marketing-retail-strategies/). Why? Wharton School research found that referred customers deliver [16-25 percent higher lifetime value](https://faculty.wharton.upenn.edu/wp-content/uploads/2012/04/Schmitt-Skiera-vandenBulte-2011-Referral-Programs-Customer-Value.pdf) than those acquired through traditional channels. They convert faster, spend more, and demonstrate significantly stronger loyalty.

A study by impact.com revealed an even more striking statistic: [86 percent of consumers](https://impact.com/research-reports/state-referral-marketing-consumers-refr-rrt-adv-ed-nam-0424/) consider personal recommendations crucial in their purchasing decisions, compared to a mere 2 percent who find traditional advertisements important.

In this guide, we’ll go beyond the “why” to unpack **six proven strategies** for [building a **referral marketing program**](https://impact.com/referral/7-proven-strategies-for-growth/) that attracts loyal customers, scales efficiently, and strengthens brand advocacy. Learn how to turn your happiest customers into your most powerful—and cost-effective—growth channel.

##### Key takeaways from this blog

*   **Referral marketing is a high ROI growth strategy:** It turns happy customers into brand advocates, reduces acquisition costs, and brings in high-quality leads.
*   **Referred customers are more valuable:** They convert at higher rates, stay longer, and spend more than customers acquired through traditional ads.
*   **Trust beats ads every time:** [86 percent of consumers](https://impact.com/research-reports/state-referral-marketing-consumers-refr-rrt-adv-ed-nam-0424/) find recommendations important vs. 2 percent that find ads important. 
*   **It’s a cost-effective way to scale:** Businesses only pay for results, making word-of-mouth marketing predictable and scaleable.
*   **Personalization and timing matter:** Successful programs offer rewards that align with customer preferences and make sharing effortless at the right moments.
*   **Referral marketing and paid media work best together:** While referrals outperform ads in ROI, combining both strategies maximizes reach and business growth.

### The importance of referral marketing

**[Word-of-mouth marketing](https://impact.com/referral/word-of-mouth-marketing-retail-strategies/)** rewards customers for bringing in new business. Customers receive incentives, including discounts, cash, or other rewards.

A [successful referral program](https://impact.com/referral/referral-partner-program-elements-that-make-it-a-success/) includes key elements that drive effective referral marketing campaigns:

*   **Win-win rewards:** The best programs benefit both referrers and new customers.
*   **Easy sharing:** Referral links should be personalized and easy to share.
*   **Smart promotion:** Integrate referrals into email, social media, and brand websites.

![The Advocacy channel podcast series on impact.com](https://impact.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/The-Advocacy-Channel-Podcast.webp)

Check out The Advocacy Channel podcast

[Listen to podcast](https://impact.com/podcasts/the-advocacy-channel/)

### Why referral marketing is beating paid search and social media ads

Paid ads can drive immediate traffic, but they’re expensive and often deliver diminishing returns.

On the other hand, referral marketing has a lower customer acquisition cost (CAC) and generates **higher-quality leads**. A reported [86 percent of consumers](https://impact.com/research-reports/state-referral-marketing-consumers-refr-rrt-adv-ed-nam-0424/) rely on reviews and referrals when purchasing, while only 2 percent consider traditional ads.

Referral marketing is a no-brainer since it taps into the credibility of existing customers to bring in new business. Personalized referral links create a sense of ownership, increasing customers’ likelihood of sharing them.

This doesn’t mean brands should ditch paid media. Instead, combining these channels maximizes reach and effectiveness:

*   **Amplify referrals with paid ads**: Promote referral incentives to attract new customers.
*   **Retarget referral leads with ads**: Keep referred customers engaged and guide them toward conversion.
*   **Collaborate with influencers and affiliates**: Expand referral reach beyond existing customers.

A Guide to Referral Marketing for Small Businesses | Attrock 

# Referral Marketing: The Ultimate Guide for Small Businesses

By: [Gaurav Sharma](https://attrock.com/blog/author/gaurav-sharma/)

Updated On: June 26, 2025

Category: [Affiliate Marketing](https://attrock.com/blog/category/affiliate-marketing)

Word Count: 3399 words | Est. Reading Time: 23 mins

Referral marketing only works for big companies with huge customer bases.

At least, that's the misconception floating around.

The truth is that referral marketing is one of the most powerful marketing solutions small businesses can use for sustainable growth.

While big brands spend a fortune on ads, you can leverage what already makes your small business special: genuine, strong customer relationships. Since these existing customers already recommend your offerings to their friends every day, you just need to make it easy and rewarding for them.

This is a strategy that brands like Tesla, Airbnb, and Dropbox have mastered.

But before you get into referral marketing, you’ll need to understand what it is and how to get it right.

Let's find out!

Table of Contents

## What Is a Referral Marketing Program?

Referral marketing is a highly effective marketing technique to encourage existing customers to recommend a brand and its products to their connections.

Businesses lure their happy customers into actively marketing their business by rewarding their recommendations.

When you incentivize these loyal customers, you can successfully [attract more leads](https://attrock.com/lead-generation-services/) for your business.

And why does referral marketing work?

Because consumers value the opinions and recommendations of real people, be it friends or strangers, more than paid ads or branded messages.

[Referral marketing strategies](https://attrock.com/blog/referral-marketing-strategies/) leverage the power of such trust to drive more qualified leads for businesses of all kinds.

Typically, referral marketing programs are of two types.

### 1\. One-Way Referral

This is one of the most commonly used [referral program](https://attrock.com/blog/best-referral-programs/) models where the company rewards an existing customer (referrer) for recommending their store, product, or service to their friends and family.

Here’s SoFi adopting this model for its various referral marketing programs.

_Image via_ [_SoFi_](https://www.sofi.com/referral-program/)

### 2\. Two-Way Referral

As the name suggests, this type of referral marketing strategy has two-way rewards. The company offers incentives to both the referrer and the referred customers upon sign-up or when they make their first purchase.

Take a look at Athletic Greens’ refer-a-friend program. It offers exciting rewards to its existing as well as new customers.

_Image via_ [_Athletic Greens_](https://athleticgreens.com/refer-a-friend/en)

You May Also Like:

*   [Affiliate Marketing Tools that are Worth Your Time](https://attrock.com/blog/affiliate-marketing-tools/)
*   [Performance Marketing Platforms You Should Start Using](https://attrock.com/blog/performance-marketing-platforms/)

## Exactly How Does Referral Marketing Work?

Referral marketing leads to increased sales and [customer retention](https://attrock.com/blog/customer-retention-strategies/), among other things. However, to fully reap the benefits of this [digital marketing strategy](https://attrock.com/blog/b2b-digital-marketing/), you should implement it properly.

Here are the steps involved in starting a referral marketing campaign:

### 1\. Identify Potential Advocates

Remember, referral marketing is all about word of mouth and who you'd want to be your advocates.

It's smart to start with your existing customers, especially the loyal ones who purchase from your store repeatedly because they love your offerings. These customers will most likely refer others because they already trust your brand.

Moreover, research shows that consumers have a higher chance of trusting the recommendation of a friend or family member than a brand.

You can also segment your customer base according to order value, engagement, or customer satisfaction. This data can help guide you in identifying a referrer persona for future targeting.

### 2\. Create Irresistible Incentives

After determining your potential advocates, think about what matters most to them. Then, offer it as a referral incentive to motivate them to spread the word to their friends and family.

After all, they’re using their time and energy to actively market your brand. It’s only fair that they get something out of it.

These goodies could be in the form of discounts, cash, or freebies for both the referrer and the referred customers. This is a two-way referral model that increases participation because it’s mutually beneficial.

### 3\. Make Sharing Effortless

Once you [create your referral program](https://attrock.com/blog/how-to-start-a-referral-program/), make it easy for your advocates to share it. It shouldn’t take more than a few steps. Provide unique referral links that track exactly who refers to whom. Customers can share these via social media, email, or messaging apps.

The simpler it is, the more your customer base will participate, and the more new customers you stand to gain.

### 4\. New Customers Convert

When someone uses a referral link to make a purchase, they become a referred customer. You then use an effective referral software to automatically:

*   Validate the sale
*   Track which loyal customer made the referral
*   Trigger the appropriate rewards

### 5\. Reward Everyone Instantly

The system automatically delivers the promised referral incentive to the original customer — the referrer. It also rewards the new customer, often with a welcome bonus. You don’t have to lift a finger or handle any manual tasks to make it happen.

### 6\. The Cycle Repeats

As more satisfied customers participate, your customer base grows organically and [brand awareness spreads](https://attrock.com/blog/build-brand-awareness/) through trusted recommendations. In the process, you gain high-value customers who stay longer.

*   [ShareASale Alternatives: Best Picks for Affiliate Success](https://attrock.com/blog/shareasale-alternatives/)
*   [Referral Marketing Software to Grow Your Business Revenue](https://attrock.com/blog/referral-marketing-software/)

## Benefits of Referral Marketing

Now that you understand how to start a referral program, let’s discuss why you should be doing it in the first place. Aside from revenue and customer retention, what are the benefits of referral marketing?

Let's take a quick look.

### 1\. Save Money on Customer Acquisition

As the competition gets tough, your customer acquisition cost keeps increasing. When compared to paid ads and [social media marketing](https://attrock.com/blog/low-cost-social-media-marketing/), refer-a-friend programs are a lot more cost-effective.

The rewards or incentives
